descriptions: Connects a workspace to Apache Iceberg source data using its configured storage and catalog settings.
descriptions./properties/spec: Choose these settings when you create the connection. To change them, create a new connection in the workspace.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/catalog: Lets a REST catalog resolve Iceberg table names to metadata files within the storage scope. Use it when readers must select by namespace and table.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/catalog/prop: Limits which catalog namespaces readers can select. List the permitted namespaces, with each namespace expressed as its sequence of name segments.
Selects the authentication method for catalog requests. Use anonymous for a catalog that permits unauthenticated reads. Use bearer when it requires the catalog-token from the source Secret.
Sets the HTTPS base URL of the REST catalog. Use the approved catalog address, including its base path, when a catalog resolves table names.
Names the installation’s endpoint policy for the REST catalog. Ask the operator which policy permits the selected catalog address.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/credentialsS: Selects the source credentials for storage reads. Bearer authentication to a REST catalog also reads its token from this Secret.
Names the Secret in this workspace. Choose the Secret with credentials for the selected backend and expected source principal.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/metadataPath: Points directly to an Iceberg table metadata JSON file, relative to the storage prefix. Choose this mode for a known metadata file. Omit it when a REST catalog resolves tables.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/storage: Sets the storage identity and the outer limit on the objects this connection may read. Use a separate connection for tables outside that location.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/storage/prop: Selects the storage API and credential format. Use s3 for Amazon S3 or gcs for Google Cloud Storage.
Names the bucket that contains the source table objects. Select the actual storage bucket even when a REST catalog supplies the table location.
Identifies the principal for storage reads. Use the source AWS role ARN for S3 or the Google service account email for GCS.
Limits file reads to this key prefix within the bucket. Use a trailing slash for a directory prefix. Use an empty string for the bucket root.
Selects the Region for S3 requests. Use the bucket’s AWS Region for S3. Omit this field for GCS.
descriptions./properties/status: Reports the configuration and runtime last observed by the provider controller. Read it when a table cannot start a scan.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/conditions: Controller observations about configuration, credential binding, runtime readiness, and admission. Read the entry for the question you need to answer.
Time when the boolean status last changed. This can stay the same across reconciliations.
Additional human-readable detail. The shared controller writes an empty message and supplies its explanation through reason.
Connection generation evaluated for this condition. Compare it with metadata.generation before acting on the result.

Names the observation. Use the type to find one condition regardless of list order.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/configDige: Identifies the resolved connection configuration. Compare the digest when checking which source configuration a runtime serves.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/observedGe: The connection generation observed on the last full reconciliation. Compare it with metadata.generation. After a validation failure, also check each condition’s generation.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/releasedEp: Admission epoch acknowledged after the controller removes the managed runtime resources. Inspect it when a disabled connection is being released.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/resolvedCo: Lists resolved configuration references. These controller versions publish an empty list. Check CredentialsValid for the outcome of credential reference validation.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/rootUIDs: Records the Kubernetes UIDs of the connection’s NetworkPolicy, Service, and Deployment. The controller uses these identities to verify ownership before changing or deleting resources.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/runtime: Identifies the runtime endpoint and reports admission and readiness. Use it to distinguish a missing runtime from a pool closed to new scans.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/runtime/pr: Whether new scans may enter the runtime pool. Inspect this flag when pods are ready but new requests are blocked.
Current control epoch reported by the runtime pool. Compare epochs when investigating stale scan admission during a drain.
UID of the runtime Deployment. Compare it with the Deployment in the workspace when checking a rollout.
Service port for requests to the connector runtime. Use it with the Service name when checking endpoint routing.
Connector protocol major version spoken by the runtime. Check it when diagnosing an incompatible client.
Identifier of the provider serving this connection. Use it to confirm the controller selected the expected connector.
Major version of the deployed provider. Admission checks it against the requested release before accepting new scans.
Count of ready runtime pods with a release label that are not terminating. Check this when RuntimeReady is false.
Distinct release versions found on ready runtime pods. Inspect this list when a rollout still serves multiple versions.
Kubernetes Service name in the workspace that routes requests to the runtime pods.
UID of the runtime Service observed by the controller. Compare it when checking whether the Service was replaced.

descriptions: A Graph defines the tables and relationships that a query or graph snapshot can use.
descriptions./properties/spec: Selects workspace Tables by alias and defines the relations between their rows.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/relations:
Defines the links between tables. Add a relation when one table holds an identifier for a row
in another, such as an order's customer identifier.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/relations/it: A directed relationship between rows in two graph tables.

Table alias and primary-key column to match against the source value.
For an order-to-customer relation, select the primary key of the customers table.

Name of an `Id` column in the aliased table. Use its foreign key at the source
and its primary key at the destination. Both columns must have the same physical type.
Alias from `spec.tables` for this end of the relation.

Use `Error` to fail the graph snapshot build on an unmatched non-null key.
Use `Warning` to allow the build to continue and report the missing matches.

Unique relation name within the graph. Use different names for different roles,
such as billing customer and delivery customer.

Table alias and foreign-key column that refer to a destination row.
For an order-to-customer relation, select the customer identifier in the orders table.

Name of an `Id` column in the aliased table. Use its foreign key at the source
and its primary key at the destination. Both columns must have the same physical type.
Alias from `spec.tables` for this end of the relation.

Use the recorded media type to identify the artifact representation.

memory.

Set the dropout probability during training. Raise it when testing stronger
regularization.

a longer plateau.

descriptions: Configures a Ballista scheduler and its executors for distributed workloads.
descriptions./properties/spec: Configure the scheduler and executor capacity that distributed jobs can use.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/artifactStor:
Select the workspace ArtifactStore named `default` for distributed inputs and outputs.
The store must be ready before the cluster can use it.
Kubernetes name of the referenced object in the same namespace. Use its `metadata.name`.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/capacity:
Controls when scheduler and executor pods run. Omit this block to keep fixed capacity,
or use it for on-demand operation.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/capacity/pro:
Idle period before an on-demand cluster drains. Use a longer interval for bursts of work
to reduce repeated cold starts.

AlwaysOn keeps the scheduler and executors running. OnDemand starts them for admitted
work and drains them after idle time.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/executor:
Sets execution slots, memory pool size, and Kubernetes resources for each executor. Size
one executor before selecting how many replicas to run.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/executor/pro:
Memory budget for an executor's query memory pool. Size it below the container memory
limit to leave room for process overhead.

Sets Kubernetes resource requests and limits for each Ballista executor. Allow room for
the configured memory pool and execution slots.

Set the CPU or memory ceiling for the workload. Choose limits that fit the namespace
quota and allow the work to complete.

Set the minimum CPU and memory that the Kubernetes scheduler must reserve for the
workload.

Number of execution slots advertised by one executor. Select a value that its CPU
allocation can sustain.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/executorImag:
Container image used by executor pods. Select the executor image published for the
specified Ballista release when provisioning the cluster.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/executorRepl:
Number of executor pods when the cluster is active. Choose more executors at
provisioning time for workloads with more parallel work.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/maxConcurren:
Bounds simultaneous producing workloads. Match the Ballista concurrency setting in the
workspace execution policy so both enforce the same limit.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/probeResourc:
Sets Kubernetes resource requests and limits for the Ballista readiness probe. Adjust
these when the probe itself cannot be scheduled or lacks resources for its test query.

Set the CPU or memory ceiling for the workload. Choose limits that fit the namespace
quota and allow the work to complete.

Set the minimum CPU and memory that the Kubernetes scheduler must reserve for the
workload.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/release:
Pins the Ballista runtime contract. This CRD requires 54.1.0. Select compatible
scheduler and executor images for that release.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/schedulerIma:
Container image used by the scheduler pod. Select the scheduler image published for the
specified Ballista release.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/schedulerRes:
Sets Kubernetes resource requests and limits for the Ballista scheduler. Size the
scheduler separately from the executors that process partitions.

Set the CPU or memory ceiling for the workload. Choose limits that fit the namespace
quota and allow the work to complete.

Set the minimum CPU and memory that the Kubernetes scheduler must reserve for the
workload.

active executors while avoiding excessive small tasks.

Exactly one activation named default per installation namespace. Secret references
are local to that namespace; private key material never belongs in spec or status.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/credentialSe:
Locates the installation credential used to activate the license. Reference the Secret
provisioned for this installation.
Kubernetes name of the referenced object in the same namespace. Use its `metadata.name`.
descriptions./properties/spec/properties/entitlementS:
Selects where the controller stores the signed entitlement returned by the license
service. The installation uses it to authorize licensed work.
Kubernetes name of the referenced object in the same namespace. Use its `metadata.name`.

Locates the installation's signing identity. Preserve this reference so the installation
can prove the same identity during renewal.
Kubernetes name of the referenced object in the same namespace. Use its `metadata.name`.

HTTPS URL of the license service for activation and renewal. Use the endpoint
provisioned for this installation.

challenge.

when completing activation.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/expiresAt: Time the current entitlement expires. Check it when activation or renewal is delayed.

this installation.

renewal.

controller.narrative:
Read `status.phase`, `status.reason`, and `status.message` to track the capture. The capture has its own outcome, separate from the profiled workload.

| Phase or reason | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| `Armed`, `Capturing`, `Finalizing` | The controller has prepared the capture, is collecting data, or is processing the result. Check `status.identity` when present to confirm the target pod and container. |
| `Ready` | The capture completed. Use `status.artifact` for the stored profile. A successful CPU export also supplies `status.flamegraph`. |
| `Partial` | Inspect the reason before using the profile. For `NoSamplesInSelectedWindow`, choose a window when the target process is active. For `CollectorExitedBeforeWindow`, the CPU collector stopped early. Check `status.artifact` for a partial profile. |
| `Unsupported` | For `ProfilingDisabled`, check installation profiling settings. For a CPU capture with `NoRunningTarget`, check whether the target pod and container are running. With `AmbiguousTargetSelectPodAndContainer`, specify the pod and container to select one target. For `CudaCaptureToolingUnavailable`, check the training target and installed CUDA profiling tools. Use step-based triggers for `CaptureTriggerUnsupported`. For `CaptureMustBeArmedBeforeLaunch`, request CUDA capture before the initial training plan is frozen. |
| `Failed` | Inspect the reason. `CollectorJobDisappeared` means the collector Job was lost. For `CaptureExportFailed`, inspect the collector result and artifact storage access. |
| `Cancelled` | The controller stopped the capture. Check `status.cleanupComplete` for cleanup of the capture resources. |

For a CUDA capture, the controller can copy the reason from the worker receipt. Read the reason and inspect the target training attempt.

A terminal phase can appear before cleanup finishes. If the reason is `CaptureLaunchUnresolved`, the controller retains the cleanup finalizer until it can establish the outcome of the collector launch.

descriptions./properties/status/properties/observedGe: The connection generation observed on the last full reconciliation. Compare it with metadata.generation. After a validation failure, also check each condition’s generation.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/releasedEp: Admission epoch acknowledged after the controller removes the managed runtime resources. Inspect it when a disabled connection is being released.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/resolvedCo: Lists resolved configuration references. These controller versions publish an empty list. Check CredentialsValid for the outcome of credential reference validation.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/rootUIDs: Records the Kubernetes UIDs of the connection’s NetworkPolicy, Service, and Deployment. The controller uses these identities to verify ownership before changing or deleting resources.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/runtime: Identifies the runtime endpoint and reports admission and readiness. Use it to distinguish a missing runtime from a pool closed to new scans.
descriptions./properties/status/properties/runtime/pr: Whether new scans may enter the runtime pool. Inspect this flag when pods are ready but new requests are blocked.
Current control epoch reported by the runtime pool. Compare epochs when investigating stale scan admission during a drain.
UID of the runtime Deployment. Compare it with the Deployment in the workspace when checking a rollout.
Service port for requests to the connector runtime. Use it with the Service name when checking endpoint routing.
Connector protocol major version spoken by the runtime. Check it when diagnosing an incompatible client.
Identifier of the provider serving this connection. Use it to confirm the controller selected the expected connector.
Major version of the deployed provider. Admission checks it against the requested release before accepting new scans.
Count of ready runtime pods with a release label that are not terminating. Check this when RuntimeReady is false.
Distinct release versions found on ready runtime pods. Inspect this list when a rollout still serves multiple versions.
Kubernetes Service name in the workspace that routes requests to the runtime pods.
UID of the runtime Service observed by the controller. Compare it when checking whether the Service was replaced.

conditions.meaning: Reports whether the controller accepted the connection configuration. Compare the condition’s observed generation with the resource generation.
Reports whether the controller accepted the source credential reference, when the configuration requires one. A connection probe tests access to the source.
Reports whether at least one runtime pod is ready. Read status.runtime.readyReplicas for the count.
Reports whether the workspace can start a new scan on this runtime. Existing work can continue during a drain.
